title: Trustworthy AI Helper - Trace the Data & Plan Checks (Part 2 Core)
summary: Students trace how the data driving their helper shapes its outcome, then plan a trusted-source verification and a risk check before trusting it.
objectives: Explain how the data used influences the helper's outcome, and predict a data change's effect.
Plan how you will verify the output and check for basic risks before trusting it.

body: Your helper works - now make sure it can be trusted. Today you trace how the data shapes its outcome and plan how you will verify it and check its risks.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can explain how the data shapes my helper's outcome and predict a change.
I can plan a verification and a risk check for my helper.

terms.definition: To follow how the data leads to the outcome.
To check a claim against a trusted, independent source.
A way the output could be wrong, unsafe, biased, or a privacy problem.

sections.heading: The data drives the outcome
body: Change the data and the outcome changes. So you can [[trace]] which data drives which part of the output.
Knowing this helps you trust - or fix - your helper.

sections.heading: Plan your checks
body: Verification checks a claim against a trusted source - not by asking the AI again.
A [[risk]] check asks: could this be wrong, unsafe, biased, or a privacy problem, and how would I reduce it?

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
body: Trace the data's influence, then plan your verification and risk check.
items: Name the data that drives one part of your output.
Predict how a data change would alter the outcome.
Choose a claim to verify against a trusted source.
Name one risk and a way to reduce it.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: How does your data shape your outcome?
What is the most trustworthy way to verify a claim?
What is your helper's biggest risk?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: The data that most shapes my outcome is ...
My top risk is ... and I will reduce it by ...

worksheet.title: Week 6 - Core - Worksheet | Trustworthy AI Helper - Trace the Data & Plan Checks (Part 2 Core)

questions.prompt: Trace the data: explain how the data influences your outcome and predict a change.
questions.stem:
The data ... drives the outcome because ...
If the data changed to ..., the outcome would ...
questions.lookFor: A specific data-to-outcome link plus a prediction - names which data drives which part of the output and says how the outcome would change if that data changed (model: the survey's most-picked genre drove the book suggestion; swapping in a class that prefers science would change the suggestion to a science book).

questions.prompt: Plan your checks: plan a verification and a risk check.
questions.stem:
Claim to verify: ... | trusted source: ...
Risk: ... | how I will reduce it: ...
questions.lookFor: The verification must use a trusted, independent source rather than the same tool, and the named risk must come with a mitigation (model: verify 'most pupils prefer adventure' against the survey totals; risk of a duplicate biasing the suggestion, reduced by de-duplicating the data).

questions.prompt: Trustworthy AI Helper Log - Part 2 (trace + check plan): record your data trace and your verification and risk plan.
questions.stem: Data -> outcome link | Verification plan | Risk + mitigation
questions.lookFor: The Core section of the Log is the assessment evidence. Mastery: explains the data's influence on the outcome, predicts a data change, and plans a trusted-source verification and a risk check with a mitigation. Partial: explanation or only one check planned.

questions.prompt: Exit ticket: explain how your data shapes your outcome, and name one claim you will verify and one risk you will reduce.
questions.lookFor: Links the data to the outcome, names one claim to be verified against a trusted source, and names one risk together with how it will be reduced.

questions.prompt: Challenge (stretch): find the single data change that would most alter your helper's outcome, and explain why it matters most.
questions.lookFor: Identifies the single data change with the largest effect and justifies it.
